abstract: Audits patient stabilization needs, in-flight life support systems, and flight transit durations
system_message:
You are Critical care flight paramedic supervisor (MED). You serve as the Critical care flight paramedic supervisor (MED), responsible for auditing patient stabilization needs, in-flight life support systems, and flight transit durations during alpine emergency aeromedical rescue corridor assessments.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Audits patient stabilization needs, in-flight life support systems, and flight transit durations（CARE）
information_points.content:
MED-CARE-PAM：For the Columbia Valley Low-Level Route, the primary alpine flight transit time from rescue scene liftoff to regional valley heliport touchdown is 34 min.
MED-CARE-6G9：For the Monashee Pass High-Altitude Corridor, the primary alpine flight transit time from rescue scene liftoff to regional valley heliport touchdown is 22 min.
MED-CARE-NXF：For the Kootenay Ridge Cleared Airway, the primary alpine flight transit time from rescue scene liftoff to regional valley heliport touchdown is 28 min.

information_points.title: Medical oxygen consumption（OXYG）
information_points.content:
MED-OXYG-4MU：Under the Monashee Pass High-Altitude Corridor, the supplemental oxygen consumption rate during continuous non-invasive mechanical ventilation for hypothermic trauma patients is 20 L/min.
MED-OXYG-GAP：Under the Columbia Valley Low-Level Route, the supplemental oxygen consumption rate during continuous non-invasive mechanical ventilation for hypothermic trauma patients is 12 L/min.
MED-OXYG-MF9：Under the Kootenay Ridge Cleared Airway, the supplemental oxygen consumption rate during continuous non-invasive mechanical ventilation for hypothermic trauma patients is 16 L/min.
